appraisal_events.evidence: mon neveu Saint-Loup est à la rigueur un bon camarade pour vous... lui c'est un homme, ce n'est pas un de ces efféminés... Il n'est pas comme les autres, il est très gentil, très sérieux.
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus singles out Saint-Loup as a genuine, serious, un-effeminate companion, favorably distinguishing him from the 'petites fripouilles' and 'efféminés' he otherwise warns the narrator against.

appraisal_events.evidence: Au point de vue de votre avenir, il ne pourra vous être utile en rien; mais pour cela, moi je suffis.
appraisal_events.explanation: Immediately after praising him personally, Charlus discounts Saint-Loup's practical usefulness for the narrator's social advancement, subordinating him to Charlus's own claimed sufficiency.

status_effects.explanation: Saint-Loup is locally elevated as a decent, serious, trustworthy young man, favorably contrasted with the corrupt young men Charlus warns about.
Charlus explicitly denies Saint-Loup any practical usefulness for the narrator's social advancement, positioning himself as the sole effective source of that advantage.

ambiguities: The narrator's amused smile at Charlus's use of the word 'sérieux' registers mild irony about Charlus's diction and manner, but does not clearly negate the substance of the praise of Saint-Loup, so E1's stance is read as neutral_report rather than ironized.
